Pharma Policy.content:
Key Points
A Medicare Part D premium subsidy program will end in 2027.
Medicare Part D premiums may rise by more than you're used to next year.
Use the Open Enrollment Period to shop around for your most affordable Part D plan for 2027.
The $23,760 Social Security bonus most retirees completely overlook ›
&&
Medicare beneficiaries could face a bit of sticker shock next year when paying for their Part D plans, as the Center for Medicare & Medicaid Services has announced that it will end a subsidy program that helped keep premiums manageable for those with stand-alone drug plans. The changes will take effect in January 2027.
This could be alarming for those already struggling with their
retirement healthcare costs
. But there are steps you can take to keep your prescription drug costs under control next year.
Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again.
In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia.
For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia.
Continue »
&&
Image source: The White House.
What's changing for Medicare beneficiaries in 2027
President Donald Trump's administration has elected to end the Part D Premium Stabilization Demonstration, a temporary subsidy program that reduced Part D premiums for seniors and capped the year-over-year premium increase. This program ran from 2025 through 2026, so if you've had a Part D plan within the last couple of years, you've likely benefited from these savings.
Without the subsidies in place, Part D premiums could increase much more in 2027 than in years past. That could force you to rethink your budget and may increase your annual spending faster than you expected.
How to keep your prescription drug costs manageable in 2027
We don't know exactly how much Part D premiums will be next year, but you'll have a chance to review them during Medicare's Open Enrollment Period, which runs from Oct. 15 to Dec. 7 of this year. This is your chance to elect new coverage for next year or to switch from Original Medicare to a Medicare Advantage plan or vice versa. Use this time to compare your options and choose the plan that covers your medications at the most affordable price.
Advertisement
If you have any questions about how your Medicare Part D plan will change next year, make sure to clarify them with the plan provider. One phone call now could save you a lot of confusion and unexpected costs down the road.
You can also explore other ways to keep prescription drug costs down, such as switching to a generic version of your medication if one is available, using coupons, or comparing prices at different pharmacies. Some drug manufacturers also offer financial assistance programs to seniors or low-income families that you may qualify for.
Once you have an idea of how much you'll pay for your Part D plan premiums and other Medicare-related costs next year, you can start building out your 2027 budget. Keep in mind that
your Social Security benefits will also get a boost
next year, so that will help cover some of your extra costs.
The $23,760 Social Security bonus most retirees completely overlook
If you're like most Americans, you're a few years (or more) behind on your retirement savings. But a handful of little-known
"Social Security secrets"
could help ensure a boost in your retirement income.
One easy trick could pay you as much as $23,760 more
... each year! Once you learn how to maximize your Social Security benefits, we think you could retire confidently with the peace of mind we're all after. Join
Stock Advisor
to learn more about these strategies.

Uterine Fibroid Drugs Market Size & Growth Analysis
The global uterine fibroid drugs
market size was valued at USD 2.34 billion  and is projected to grow from USD 2.57 billion in 2026 to USD 5.41 billion by 2034, registering a CAGR of 9.77% during the forecast period 2026–2034. North America dominated the uterine fibroid drugs market
with a market
share of 43.18% in 2025.
Uterine fibroid drugs include gonadotropin releasing hormone agonists, GnRH antagonists, selective progesterone receptor modulators, NSAIDs, and other supportive medications. They help to improve quality of life, making them an important treatment option for women with minimally invasive management.
The uterine fibroid drugs market demand is increasing due to the rising prevalence of uterine fibroids, growing awareness of early diagnosis, and increasing preference for non-surgical treatment options. Continuous advancements in hormonal therapies, favorable reimbursement policies in developed countries, and ongoing clinical research are further supporting uterine fibroid drugs market growth.

Uterine Fibroid Drugs Market Trends
Increasing Adoption of Oral GnRH Antagonist Therapies
The market is shifting from injectable hormonal therapies toward convenient oral GnRH antagonist treatments that offer effective symptom control with improved patient adherence. This transition is driven by the growing preference for non-invasive, long-term medical management before considering surgery. As a result, pharmaceutical companies are expanding oral treatment portfolios and improving patient accessibility. For example, MYFEMBREE (relugolix combination therapy) by Myovant Sciences and Pfizer has gained significant adoption for managing heavy menstrual bleeding associated with uterine fibroids.
Growing Preference for Fertility Preserving Non-Surgical Treatment
Women are increasingly opting for drug-based therapies that control fibroid symptoms while preserving fertility and avoiding invasive procedures. This shift is supported by rising awareness, earlier diagnosis, and advances in targeted hormonal therapies that delay or reduce the need for surgery. Consequently, demand for innovative pharmaceutical treatments continues to expand across reproductive-age women.

Impact of Supply Chain Disruption on Uterine Fibroid Drugs Market
The Uterine Fibroid Drugs Market is indirectly exposed to supply chain disruptions due to its reliance on active pharmaceutical ingredients, specialized excipients, contract manufacturing organizations, and global pharmaceutical distribution networks. Disruptions in raw material sourcing, manufacturing operations, and international logistics can delay drug production, limit product availability, and increase procurement costs, affecting both branded and generic therapies across multiple regions. The market is demonstrating a capacity-constrained recovery, supported by stabilized API supplies, expanded production capabilities, and continued investments in supply chain resilience and pharmaceutical manufacturing infrastructure.
Uterine Fibroid Drugs Market Dynamics
Market Drivers
Increasing Clinical Adoption of Combination Therapies and Rising Adoption of Patient-specific Hormonal Treatment Drives Market
The development of combination therapies that balance symptom control with improved safety profiles is driving demand for advanced uterine fibroid drugs. These treatments help manage heavy menstrual bleeding, reduce anemia-related complications, and delay invasive procedures such as myomectomy or hysterectomy. As physicians increasingly prioritize medical management before surgery, adoption of pharmacological therapies is increasing across gynecology practices.
The shift toward personalized treatment strategies based on fibroid severity, symptom burden, and reproductive goals is increasing demand for targeted uterine fibroid drugs. Physicians are increasingly selecting therapies with adjustable dosing and improved tolerability to address diverse patient needs, particularly among women seeking to preserve fertility. For example, relugolix combination therapies provide clinicians with an option to manage moderate-to-severe fibroid symptoms while considering long-term treatment requirements.
Market Restraints
Side Effects and Competition from Minimally Invasive Procedures Restrain Market Expansion
Hormonal therapies used for uterine fibroid management can cause adverse effects such as hot flashes, bone mineral density reduction, and hormonal imbalances, limiting long-term treatment use. For example, GnRH agonists such as leuprolide acetate are generally recommended for short-term use due to risks of bone mineral density loss with extended therapy. These safety concerns require monitoring and may influence physician decisions, creating a restraint on prolonged adoption of hormonal fibroid treatments.
Advancements in minimally invasive procedures, including uterine artery embolization (UAE) and magnetic resonance guided focused ultrasound surgery, provide effective alternatives for managing symptomatic uterine fibroids without prolonged drug use. These procedures can offer faster symptom improvement and reduce dependence on continuous hormonal therapies.
Market Opportunities
Expansion of Fertility-focused Fibroid Drug Therapies and Development of Novel Non-Hormonal & Targeted Fibroid Therapies Offer Growth Opportunities
The growing focus on fertility preservation creates an opportunity for pharmaceutical companies developing uterine fibroid therapies that control symptoms while delaying or avoiding invasive procedures. This opportunity is particularly relevant for companies investing in hormonal therapies with improved safety profiles for younger women seeking pregnancy options. Future market growth is expected as personalized treatment approaches and fertility-preserving care pathways become more common. Companies such as Myovant Sciences, Pfizer, and Theramex are expanding their women’s health portfolios around advanced hormonal treatments for symptomatic fibroids.
The demand for safer long-term treatment options creates growth opportunities for drug developers working on targeted and non-hormonal approaches that overcome limitations of existing hormonal therapies. This opportunity is driving research into therapies that directly address fibroid growth pathways while reducing adverse effects. Future adoption is expected to increase as clinical validation supports broader use of innovative treatments.
Market Challenges
Complex Disease Variability and Limited Patient Identification Challenges Market Growth
The heterogeneous nature of uterine fibroids, with differences in size, location, number, and biological characteristics, creates challenges in developing therapies with consistent outcomes across patients. For example, treatments such as GnRH-based therapies may effectively reduce heavy menstrual bleeding but show variable effects on fibroid size reduction among different patients. This variability increases clinical trial complexity, requires patient-specific evaluation, and slows the development of broadly effective uterine fibroid drugs.
Another key challenge for the uterine fibroid drugs market is the delayed identification of eligible patients due to asymptomatic cases, underdiagnosis, and limited screening practices. Many women seek treatment only after symptoms become severe, reducing opportunities for early pharmacological intervention. For example, women with mild fibroid symptoms may remain untreated until heavy menstrual bleeding or anemia develops, limiting the addressable patient pool for drug therapies.

Pharma Policy.content:
A man allegedly fled from the police on a motorcycle and got into an accident with a car in Farrer Road on Aug. 18.
The 37-year-old man was arrested.
He was found with a vaporiser and pod.
A 26-year-old pillion rider was found to be in possession of substances believed to be controlled drugs.
What eyewitnesses saw
A
Shin Min Daily News
reader took photos in the aftermath of the accident.
An eyewitness told
Shin Min
that a motorcycle was wedged under a car and two men were lying on the ground.
She said the motorcycle knocked down two small trees before colliding with a car.
A substance, believed to be blood, as well as debris, were seen on the road.
At least two traffic police motorcycles were at the scene.
Stopped during police patrol
A traffic police officer on patrol had signalled for the motorcyclist to stop for a check at about 5pm on Aug. 18 along Adam Road.
The man sped off instead and officers gave chase.
The motorcycle skidded during pursuit and got into an accident with a car.
The motorcyclist and his pillion rider were conscious when taken to the National University Hospital, the police and the Singapore Civil Defence Force said.
The motorcyclist was arrested for dangerous driving and driving without a valid licence, the police said.
He is being investigated for failing to stop when ordered by an officer and riding without insurance coverage.
The vaporiser-related offence has been referred to the Health Sciences Authority.
The suspected drug-related offence will be dealt with by the Central Narcotics Bureau, police said.

The government says a royally-donated cancer drug has reached 215 patients so far. That’s out of 4,420 registered to receive it. Distribution continues toward a target of 23,000 boxes by October.
Deputy government spokesperson Ploythale Laksameesangchan said on August 21 that the National Health Security Office (NHSO) has so far delivered 2,880 boxes of the drug, IMCRANIB, to Lopburi Cancer Hospital, Chulabhorn Hospital, the National Cancer Institute, and Rajavithi Hospital.
Three more shipments are planned to reach the full 23,000 boxes by the end of October. That will expand access for cancer patients under Thailand’s universal healthcare scheme, commonly known as the Gold Card.
IMCRANIB is an oral targeted cancer therapy containing imatinib. It’s used to treat chronic myeloid leukaemia (CML) and gastrointestinal stromal tumours (GIST), a cancer that develops in the muscle layer of the digestive tract.
The drug was donated through NHSO by Professor Dr. HRH Princess Chulabhorn Krom Phra Srisavangavadhana. She provided 690,000 tablets, or 23,000 boxes, to be distributed to hospitals nationwide. The donation gives patients across the country free access to an effective cancer treatment. It also eases the financial burden on patients and their families.
Ploythale said the Chulabhorn Royal Academy will be able to produce imatinib in both 100mg and 400mg doses, starting in the 2027 fiscal year. That will let doctors choose the dosage that best fits each patient’s treatment plan. It should make the medication easier to take, and help patients stay on treatment continuously.
“This distribution of royally-donated medicine is another key mechanism that expands access to treatment, eases the financial burden on patients and their families, and strengthens the security of the medicine supply, so the universal health coverage system can care for cancer patients,” Ploythale said.

Updated On Aug 22, 2026 at 07:20 AM IST
New Delhi: The Union Health Ministry is planning to reclassify four off-patent central nervous system (CNS) drugs —flupentixol,
zopiclone
, gabapentin and carisoprodol— to bring them under closer regulatory oversight amid concerns over their potential misuse.
In a gazette notification, the Ministry said the four drugs have been proposed for reclassification under Schedule H1, which would impose stricter controls and record-keeping requirements on their sale across the country.
Advt
The amendment follows a recommendation by an expert committee, which proposed the reclassification of the four drugs to the apex internal advisory body, the Drugs Consultative Committee (DCC). The recommendation was considered at the DCC’s 68th meeting in March this year.
Flupentixol, is a antipsychotic medication used to treats mental health conditions like schizophrenia and chronic psychosis. Zopiclone is a sedative-hypnotic medication, used for the short-term treatment of severe insomnia.

While both Schedule H and H1 drugs are sold through prescriptions, the latter requires retailers to maintain detailed sales records, including the details of of the prescriber and the patient.

It also mandates drug makers to add a Schedule H1 warning on the drug’s packaging.
The proposed amendment is currently in draft form and open for stakeholder comments for 30 days from the date of its publication.
Over the past few months, the Ministry has stepped up scrutiny of prescription drugs and moved several medicines to the Schedule H1 category amid growing concerns of misuse. Most recently, pregabalin, a commonly prescribed drug for neuropathic pain, was shifted to the stricter prescription category.
The drug was reclassified following reports from several state agencies flagging its misuse among young people for its sedative, euphoric and dissociative effects.

Pharma Associations.url_match_title: Government plans 2,000-acre pharmaceutical innovation park in Osudoku to boost local drug production - MyJoyOnline
Pharma Associations.content:
Audio By Carbonatix
The government is planning to establish a 2,000-acre pharmaceutical innovation park in the Osudoku area as part of efforts to reduce the country’s dependence on imported medicines and strengthen local pharmaceutical manufacturing.
The Legon Pharmaceutical Innovation Park, a flagship project under the 24-Hour Economy Authority, is expected to create an integrated ecosystem covering pharmaceutical manufacturing, medical-device production, herbal medicine, and research and development.
Head, Project Development at the 24-Hour Economy Authority, Kafui Linda Abbah-Foli, said the project is intended to address some of the major challenges facing pharmaceutical manufacturers, particularly access to land and critical infrastructure.
She said the park would provide roads, water, electricity, wastewater treatment and specialised pharmaceutical effluent treatment facilities.
“The park will provide all this bulk infrastructure facility,” she said.
According to Ms Abbah Foli, providing the infrastructure within a dedicated industrial ecosystem would make it easier for pharmaceutical manufacturers and entrepreneurs to establish and expand their operations.
The proposed park comes as Ghana continues to rely heavily on imports to meet its pharmaceutical requirements.
Ms Abbah Foli said the country currently imports about 70% of its pharmaceutical needs, including finished medicines, active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) and excipients such as starch and alcohol.
She said the park is therefore being designed to cover the pharmaceutical value chain and reduce the country's vulnerability to disruptions in global supply chains.
The initiative is also expected to support local production of medical devices, including HIV and malaria test kits, which are currently largely imported.
The Authority believes expanding domestic manufacturing capacity will improve Ghana's preparedness for future health emergencies.
“The goal is to ensure that we build a park that will cater for the whole value chain so that when we are confronted by a pandemic like COVID in the future, we will be self-sufficient,” Ms Abbah Foli said.
The Authority has completed pre-feasibility studies for the project and is preparing for a full feasibility study focusing on the design and master planning of the park.
An anchor investor is expected to partner with the government and the 24-Hour Economy Authority in developing the facility.
The Authority has also identified potential tenants, including existing pharmaceutical manufacturers in Ghana and international companies from India, China and the United States.
Ms Abbah Foli said Ghanaian health professionals living abroad had also expressed interest in the project.
She said Ghana was drawing lessons from pharmaceutical parks in India and seeking to attract some companies operating within those ecosystems to establish operations in the country.
The proposed development is expected to go beyond a conventional industrial park.
Ms Abbah Foli said the project would include housing facilities for workers and other supporting infrastructure needed to create a complete pharmaceutical ecosystem.
The Authority is targeting up to 20,000 jobs within the first five years of the park's development.
The park is also expected to accommodate herbal medicine production and research and development activities.
Land acquisition remains a key component of the project, with about 2,000 acres identified in the Osudoku area.
The Authority said it is engaging traditional authorities and communities through what it describes as a participatory land acquisition model.
Under the proposed arrangement, landowners and communities would not only receive rental income but also have the opportunity to become shareholders in the park.
“Aside from paying them their rental income, they will be shareholders in the park. So every year they get some dividends and also get some rental income,” Ms Abbah Foli said.
The model is intended to ensure that communities benefit directly from the economic activity generated by the development.
The Authority also sees the pharmaceutical park as an opportunity to respond to Ghana's changing disease burden.
While infectious diseases such as malaria remain a major public health concern, the country is also recording increasing cases of non-communicable diseases, including diabetes and stroke.
Ms Abbah Foli said the park could attract manufacturers producing medicines for these conditions, helping to reduce Ghana's dependence on imported drugs and potentially easing pressure on health expenditure.
She argued that continued reliance on imported medicines means many of the jobs, investments and economic opportunities associated with the pharmaceutical value chain are created outside Ghana.
The broader ambition, she said, is to build a stronger domestic pharmaceutical industry capable of meeting a greater share of Ghana's medicine needs while creating jobs and attracting investment.
The Authority believes the development could also strengthen Ghana's ability to maintain access to essential medicines and medical products during future global health emergencies.

Which Pharmaceutical Companies Have the Largest Global Market Share?

Which Pharmaceutical Companies Have the Largest Global Market Share?

Introduction
The global pharmaceutical industry is considered one of the most valuable and most fragmented major industries in the world economy. According to Precedence Research, the pharmaceutical market has reached $1.77 trillion in 2025 and is anticipated to nearly double to $3.20 trillion by 2035, yet even the industry's single largest firm, Eli Lilly, controls less than 4% of that total.
This report combines Precedence Research's market-sizing and segmentation data with each major firm's own FY2024 financial disclosures to answer, in detail, which pharmaceutical firms actually hold the largest global market share, alongside how that share is distributed across regions, disease categories, and even drug types, and what recent M&A activity along with the GLP-1 obesity-drug boom are doing to reshape the industry's competitive leaderboard in real time.
Key Takeaways
The pharmaceutical market worldwide was valued at $1.77 trillion in 2025 and is anticipated to reach $3.20 trillion by 2035, rising at a CAGR of 6.10%.
The top 12 pharmaceutical firms by revenue together control nearly 39% of the estimated $1.7 trillion 2024 global pharmaceutical market, a highly concentrated but not monopolistic industry structure.
Merck & Co.'s Keytruda is considered the world's best-selling drug in 2024 at $29.5 billion in sales, thus growing 18% and now accounting for roughly 46% of Merck's total revenue.
Eli Lilly became the world's largest pharmaceutical firm by revenue in FY2024 with $65.2 billion, overtaking longtime leaders for the strength of its GLP-1 obesity or diabetes franchise.
North America holds the largest regional share of the worldwide pharmaceutical market at 42% in 2025, while Asia Pacific is anticipated to be the fastest-growing region through 2035.
The U.S. pharmaceutical market alone was valued at $520.38 billion in 2025 and is estimated to reach $963.52 billion by 2035, approximately 29% of the entire global pharmaceutical market on its own.
Prescription medicines dominate the worldwide market with an 87% revenue share in 2025; meanwhile, conventional small-molecule drugs (55%) still edge out biologics and biosimilars (45%), though biologics are growing faster.
GLP-1 drugs for diabetes and obesity, including Novo Nordisk's Ozempic or Wegovy and Eli Lilly's Mounjaro or Zepbound, have become one of the fastest-growing franchises in pharmaceutical history, thus collectively approaching $50-55 billion in annual sales by 2024-2025.
Cancer is the single-largest disease category in worldwide pharmaceutical spending, generating an estimated 19% revenue share in 2025, ahead of cardiovascular disease and diabetes.
Major 2024-2025 M&A activity, including AbbVie's $8.7B ImmunoGen acquisition and Novo Holdings' $16.5B Catalent acquisition, alongside J&J's $14.6B Intra-Cellular Therapies deal, shows the industry consolidating around oncology, obesity, and even manufacturing capacity.
Visual Intelligence: 15 Data Stories on Global Pharmaceutical Market Share
Global Pharmaceutical Market Set to Nearly Double by 2035
According to Precedence Research, the worldwide
pharmaceutical market
starts at a baseline of USD 1.77 trillion in 2025, and it expands to USD 3.20 trillion by 2035. Thus, this trajectory reflects a steady compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 6.10% from 2026 through 2035, propelled by an aging demographic as well as greater
adoption of biologics
.
Key Insight
: A 6.10% compound annual growth rate sustained over a decade is a significant trajectory for a trillion-dollar-plus industry; it states the market will add more absolute value in the upcoming ten years, which is $1.43 trillion than the entire pharmaceutical market globally was worth as recently as the early 2010s.
Source: Precedence Research - "Pharmaceutical Market Size, Share and Trends 2026 to 2035 (Report Code 6227)," Updated June 23, 2026.

The top global pharmaceutical firms by FY2024 revenue include industry giants such as Pfizer, Roche, Merck & Co., Johnson & Johnson, and AbbVie. These market leaders pull in tens of billions of dollars yearly, securing significant individual slices of the overall $1.7 trillion global market. Lilly recorded $65.2 billion in total sales, good for 3.84% growth over the roughly $34 billion it pocketed in 2024.
Key Insight
: No single firm holds more than 4% of the global market - even industry leader Eli Lilly's $65.2 billion represents just 3.83% of total worldwide spending, underscoring that "market share" in pharma is completely different from concentrated industries like search or social media, where a handful of companies can control a majority of the market.
Source: Multiple (see below) - "Company FY2024 earnings releases and annual reports; market share calculated against Precedence Research's global market baseline," 2024-2025.
The Top 12 Pharmaceutical Companies Control Roughly 39% of the Global Market
In the current high-stakes biopharma landscape, being a “top pharmaceutical firm” means much more than scale. It means excelling in global revenue, market valuation, innovation pipeline, and therapeutic leadership.  The top 12 pharmaceutical firms highlight a moderately fragmented global market, where industry leaders Johnson & Johnson, Pfizer, and Roche remain global pharma leaders by combining high revenue with innovation in immunology,
oncology
, and even diagnostics.
Key Insight
: Even combined, the industry's twelve largest major players leave 60% of the worldwide market to thousands of smaller firms, generic manufacturers, and regional players, a reminder that "Big Pharma" supremacy is real at the level of individual drug categories as well as therapeutic areas.
Source: Calculated from company disclosures - "FY2024 revenue figures against Precedence Research's ~$1.7 trillion 2024 global market estimate," 2024-2025.
North America Dominates the Global Pharmaceutical Market
North America leads the global pharmaceutical market with nearly 42% revenue share in 2025, valued overall at roughly USD 1.77 trillion. Europe has 28%, and Asia Pacific has 20% revenue generation. It is driven by government support and investments in research and development, wider usage of biologics and
biosimilars
, and even increased healthcare spending, which further supports market expansion. Pharmaceutical firms are focusing on adopting cutting-edge technologies such as AI to boost the production of pharmaceuticals.
Key Insight
: North America's 42% share is disproportionate to its share of the world population, thus reflecting both higher per-capita drug pricing along with the highest-value branded and specialty drug launches in the US market, while Asia Pacific's rapid growth trajectory suggests the regional balance will change measurably over the next decade.
Source: Precedence Research - "Pharmaceutical Market regional insights," 2025.
Prescription Medicines Dominate the Global Pharmaceutical Market
The global pharmaceutical market was valued at nearly USD 1.77 trillion in 2025 and is predicted to exceed USD 3.20 trillion by 2035, with a CAGR of 6.10% from 2026 to 2035, with prescription medicines commanding a dominant share of roughly 84% to 86% and over-the-counter (OTC) products making up the remaining 14% to 16%.
Prescription Medicines
: It is estimated to account for an 87% share of the total market value, driven heavily by oncology, specialty therapies, and chronic disease treatments.
Over-the-Counter (OTC): It accounts for approximately 13% of global value, led by vitamins, analgesics, and cough or cold remedies.
Key Insight:
The 87/13 split explains why pharmaceutical firms concentrate marketing, along with R&D investment, on physician relationships and payer negotiations rather than consumer advertising. The OTC segment is the fastest-growing segment, despite being a small fraction of where the industry's revenue actually sits.
Source: Precedence Research - "Pharmaceutical Market segment insights, by type," 2025.
Small Molecules Still Edge Out Biologics - But Not for Long
Conventional small-molecule drugs generally hold the dominant market share at roughly 55%, while biologics and biosimilars account for the remaining 45%, according to Precedence Research, which highlights faster growth rates for large-molecule biologics.
Small Molecules
: They represent about 55% of the global market, which is favored for oral administration, low production costs, and generic availability.
Biologics & Biosimilars
: They represent around 45% of the market, propelled by high need for targeted oncology and immunology treatments.
Key Insight
: The near-even 55/45 split marks an inflection point the industry has now been approaching for two decades, as biologics and biosimilars are the faster-growing segment. This creates a balance that will likely tip toward large-molecule drugs within the next several forecast years, with major implications for manufacturing infrastructure investment.
Source: Precedence Research - "Pharmaceutical Market segment insights, by molecule type," 2025.
Cancer Is the Single Largest Disease Category in Global Pharma Spending
This chart breaks down the worldwide pharmaceutical market by major disease category:
Cancer:
The single largest therapeutic segment, thus capturing nearly 19% of total global pharmaceutical revenues, driven by immunotherapies, expensive targeted therapies, and
precision medicine
.
Cardiovascular Diseases: It retains massive prescription volume because many primary-care heart medications are low-cost generics.
Diabetes:
It is rapidly expanding due to the commercial explosion of GLP-1 receptor agonists for diabetes as well as weight management.
Key Insight
: Cancer's 19% share is the largest of any single disease category, which reflects both the high price points of modern oncology drugs and the sheer volume of new cancer diagnoses globally.
Source: Precedence Research - "Pharmaceutical Market segment insights, by disease," 2025.
Oral Medications Remain the Preferred Route of Administration Worldwide
This chart shows the global pharmaceutical market split by route of administration.
Oral accounts for nearly 58% of the pharmaceutical market because of patient comfort, low production costs, and easy storage.
Parenteral (injectable) medications account for a large share, usually around 30% or more, of the pharmaceutical market because they bypass the digestive system, providing high effectiveness, fast results, and even a way to deliver complex drugs that pills cannot handle.
Key Insight
: Oral formulations, which account for roughly 58% of the share, reflect patient preference and lower administration expenses, but the designation of parenteral (injectable) as the fastest-growing route directly tracks the GLP-1 boom; both Ozempic and Mounjaro are injectable therapies. Route-of-administration trends are now being reshaped by a single, extraordinarily successful drug class.
Source: Precedence Research - "Pharmaceutical Market segment insights, by route of administration," 2025.

The GLP-1 Obesity - Diabetes Drug Boom Is Reshaping Pharma's Revenue Leaderboard
Between 2022 and 2025, Eli Lilly experienced an explosive revenue surge, achieving annual growth in 2025, largely driven by the rapid market penetration of Mounjaro and Zepbound. Thus, Novo Nordisk sustained steady, fast growth with Ozempic and Wegovy, though Lilly aggressively narrowed the gap via its dual-agonist tirzepatide portfolio.
Eli Lilly (Mounjaro & Zepbound): It is fueled by hyper-demand for tirzepatide, scaling quarterly sales past a billion and driving Lilly's total full-year 2025.
Novo Nordisk (Ozempic & Wegovy): It retained massive global prescription volumes, thus expanding overall sales into the hundreds of billions of Danish kroner despite rising competitive pressure.
Key Insight
: Eli Lilly's GLP-1 franchise grew approximately tenfold in three years, an expansion rate almost unheard of at this revenue scale in the pharmaceutical industry's history. Thus, this single drug class is now large enough to have the total pharmaceutical revenue of many mid-sized firms profiled elsewhere in this report.
Source: Eli Lilly and Company; Novo Nordisk A/S - "Company earnings releases, 2022-2025 (2025 figures are illustrative estimates based on reported trajectories)," 2022-2025.

R&D discovery: It targets ID, drug candidate screening, and preclinical testing.
Clinical trials: They have three phases- Phase 1 trials: Small groups of healthy people test the drug for safety and safe dosage levels.
Phase 2 and 3 trials: Larger groups of patients test the drug for effectiveness and side effects compared to standard treatments.
Regulatory approval: Government agencies review all trial data before allowing market release.
Manufacturing: It deals with production, GMP formulation, and quality control.
Distribution: It includes wholesalers, hospitals, and retail pharmacies. Patient treatment: It covers Prescription and treatment delivery.
Key Insight
: Unlike many other industries, pharmaceutical "market share" is generally earned or lost mainly at the R&D and clinical-trial stages, years or even decades before a product generates any revenue, meaning current's revenue rankings largely reflect strategic R&D and licensing decisions made in the 2010s.
Source: Precedence Research - "Pharmaceutical Market Value Chain Analysis," 2025.
Hospital Pharmacies Are the Leading Distribution Channel Globally
This chart shows the worldwide pharmaceutical market split by distribution channel: hospital pharmacy versus retail pharmacy and other channels.
Hospital pharmacy accounts for 54% and focuses on acute inpatient care, complex compounding, along with direct coordination with medical teams, while retail pharmacy accounts for 46% as it serves community outpatients, over-the-counter sales, and even routine preventive medicine.
Key Insight
: Hospital pharmacies are in the leading position, reflecting the rising share of complex, physician-administered specialty and even injectable drugs, which include many oncology and GLP-1 therapies, that cannot be self-administered or picked up at a standard retail counter. It is a structural shift favoring firms with strong hospital-system relationships and even specialty distribution networks.
Source: Precedence Research - "Pharmaceutical Market segment insights, by distribution channel," 2025.
The U.S. Remains the World's Largest National Pharmaceutical Market
The U.S. pharmaceutical market size is expected to reach USD 520.38 billion in 2025 and is anticipated to increase from USD 552.72 billion in 2026 to nearly USD 963.52 billion by 2035, expanding at a CAGR of 6.35% from 2026 to 2035. The market shows substantial growth due to the rising need for personalized and regenerative therapies for chronic diseases. Further, the expansion is propelled by technological advancements and the integration of AI and machine learning, which will accelerate R&D and drug discovery in the upcoming years.
Key Insight
: A single country generating nearly 29% of global pharmaceutical revenue is a remarkable concentration. It explains why nearly every major pharmaceutical firm treats US regulatory and reimbursement policy, including the Inflation Reduction Act's drug-pricing provisions, as an existential strategic issue rather than a routine market-specific consideration.
Source: Precedence Research - "U.S. Pharmaceutical Market" regional report, 2025-2035 forecast.

Key Companies & Organizations
Top-Tier Global Companies (FY2024 Revenue >$55B)
Eli Lilly and Company has reached a historic milestone as the first pharmaceutical company to cross a $1 trillion market cap, driven by a 45% surge in 2025 revenue to $65.2 billion, fueled by blockbuster GLP-1 medications such as Mounjaro and Zepbound.
Merck & Co., Inc. has $64.17B in market revenue. Its primary growth drivers remain its significant oncology immunotherapy Keytruda and its HPV vaccine Gardasil, along with recent late-stage pipeline growth in personalized mRNA cancer vaccines.
Pfizer Inc. reported $62.6 billion in total revenue, driven by major non-COVID growth products such as Eliquis, the Vyndaqel family, and even the Comirnaty COVID-19 vaccine.
AbbVie Inc. achieved nearly $61.2 billion in annual revenue, propelled by its post-Humira immunology Skyrizi and Rinvoq, which thus successfully offset ongoing biosimilar declines.
AstraZeneca PLC registered total revenue of $58.7 billion for fiscal year 2025, driven by a broad portfolio that includes blockbusters such as Farxiga, Tagrisso, and Imfinzi.
Major Global Companies (FY2024 Revenue $40B-$55B)
Novartis AG is a major global healthcare firm based in Switzerland that focuses on innovative medicines with nearly $54.5B in market capitalization.
Bristol Myers Squibb Company reported annual revenues of $48.3 billion, with its expansion-driving growth portfolio contributing $22.6 billion.
Sanofi S.A. has reported $47.92B in market revenue and is advancing targeted therapy for Dupixent, vaccines, and rare disease.
Novo Nordisk A/S has reported $42.1B in market revenue.
GSK plc has stated $40.1B in market revenue and deals with vaccines and specialty medicines.
Notable Mid-to-Large Companies

Gilead Sciences, Inc. has $28.75B in revenue in 2024. It mainly deals with HIV and antiviral treatments.
Takeda Pharmaceutical Company Limited deals with medications and treatments for oncology, rare disease, and neuroscience.
Bayer AG is a pharmaceuticals and consumer health firm and is one of the few top-20 companies with a 2024 revenue decline.
Manufacturing, Distribution & Supply Chain Partners

Pharma Associations.content:
Pharma Capital, a company belonging to Sefrioui Group, is seeking to acquire 100 per cent of Servier Maroc and Servier Maroc Investissements, according to a notification published by Morocco’s Competition Council.
The proposed transaction covers the entire share capital and voting rights of both companies. It remains subject to regulatory approval, and no purchase price has been disclosed.
Africa Intelligence reported on 19 August that Pharma Capital had outbid other candidates for the businesses. It also reported that the new owner would manufacture Servier medicines under licence for 15 years.
ADVERTISEMENT
Those details were reported by Africa Intelligence and are not contained in the Competition Council’s public notification.
DON'T MISS THIS:
Moroccan billionaire Anas Sefrioui sells French cement plant to focus on African expansion
From property into pharmaceuticals
Sefrioui built most of his fortune through Groupe Addoha, the Casablanca-listed property developer known for housing projects in Morocco and other African markets.
Forbes estimated his family’s fortune at $1.5 billion on 20 August.
ADVERTISEMENT
The Servier transaction would strengthen a pharmaceutical portfolio that Sefrioui has been building separately from his property and cement businesses.
In November 2024, Pharma Capital notified the Competition Council of a transaction involving proposed stakes of 95.35 per cent in Afric-Phar, 55 per cent in Pharmis and four per cent in Partner Lab.
Pharma Capital is seeking 100 per cent of Servier Maroc and Servier Maroc Investissements, subject to regulatory approval.
Pharmacy and healthcare spending are exposed on multiple fronts to the inflationary pressures of the war in Iran."The adhesives in bandages, the coatings on pills, the plastic in blister packs, the bottles that hold every prescription in America: all petrochemical," Malek laid out.Not only are prescription medications packaged in plastic, some of the materials themselves that go into pharmaceutical drugs are affected.The global pharmaceutical trade has been hurt by the war time disruption to commercial shipping, especially since many drugs and pharmaceutical inputs have short shelves lives meaning shipping delays compromise quality.The increased costs of prescriptions compound healthcare inflation already weighing on consumers.
Business Insider USA
The regulator described the transaction as the proposed acquisition of exclusive control of the three companies.
Afric-Phar and Pharmis manufacture and distribute pharmaceutical products, while Partner Lab specialises in pharmaceutical research and development.
ADVERTISEMENT
The Servier deal would add another manufacturing and distribution operation to that portfolio.
DON'T MISS THIS:
Moroccan billionaire Anas Sefrioui commits $300 million to luxury mixed-use project in Abidjan
What the transaction includes
Servier Maroc manufactures, distributes and markets medicines covering cardiovascular and metabolic diseases, venous conditions and oncology, according to the Competition Council.
Servier Maroc Investissements owns and manages commercial and industrial property. Its activities include acquiring, leasing, constructing and developing real estate.
ADVERTISEMENT
Pharma Capital is therefore seeking both the operating pharmaceutical company and the property associated with the business.
Servier operates in more than 130 countries and employs over 20,000 people worldwide. The foundation-controlled group generated approximately $8 billion (€6.86 billion) in revenue during its 2024/25 financial year.
The proposed sale does not include Servier’s global business or ownership of its international medicines. It concerns only the two Moroccan entities.
If the reported 15-year licensing arrangement is confirmed, the Moroccan operation would be able to continue manufacturing Servier products after the ownership change.
DON'T MISS THIS:
Africa’s billionaires add $20bn in a year as Forbes tags Femi Otedola as continent's poorest billionaire
ADVERTISEMENT
A growing pharmaceutical portfolio
The acquisition would move Sefrioui further away from his public image as mainly a property billionaire.
It would also give Pharma Capital a larger position in Morocco’s pharmaceutical manufacturing sector at a time when the country is trying to produce more medicines locally and reduce its dependence on imports.
However, neither the Competition Council nor Pharma Capital has said whether Servier Maroc would be merged with Sefrioui’s other pharmaceutical interests.
The deal must therefore be described as proposed or pending. Sefrioui has not completed the acquisition, and final regulatory approval has not been publicly announced.

August 21, 2026
Will PBMs' TrumpRx Price Pledge Reach Prescribers?
Author(s)
Stephen Appezzato
Listen
0:00
/
0:00
Key Takeaways
Ten PBMs will integrate TrumpRx cash pricing into RTBT displays, allowing prescribers and patients to compare cash-pay versus plan benefit costs at the point of prescribing.
Clinician workflow remains the key bottleneck, with RTBTs opened in 1.3%–13.5% of encounters and suggested switches accepted about 11% of the time.
Hospital and employer enablement is uneven despite Part D requirements, with only 55% of hospitals using RTBTs for all or nearly all plans as of 2025.
AMCP’s June 2026 survey showed more respondents expect TrumpRx to be unlikely to beat insurance pricing and unlikely to lower overall US drug costs.
Manufacturers with TrumpRx agreements may see channel shift toward cash-pay when prices undercut benefit costs, while nonparticipants receive no comparable RTBT visibility.
SHOW MORE
In coordination with the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services, 10 PBMs will surface TrumpRx cash prices in prescribers' benefit tools, PCMA announced.
Advertisement
Citing increased transparency, affordability and consumer choice, 10 pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs) committed to displaying TrumpRx cash prices alongside benefit pricing within Real Time Benefit Tools (RTBTs), the point-of-prescribing systems doctors use to check patient costs, in coordination with the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS). Their trade group, the Pharmaceutical Care Management Association (PCMA), announced the commitment.
1,2
The participating PBMs pledged to present the cash prices listed on TrumpRx for comparison against a patient's benefit-based price, delivered through existing RTBTs, when consistent with plan coverage and allowed by law. CMS Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz said the change would let patients see cost differences directly and choose accordingly, calling it the kind of transparency needed to spur competition and lower costs.
1
“Consumers and patients are better off when they have more options and a clear view of their costs. If there are times when a product is cheapest on TrumpRx, patients should know that,” said David Marin, president and CEO of PCMA
,
in a press release.
2
The commitment builds on PCMA's characterization of the PBM industry's longstanding investment in real-time cost tools delivered through portals and apps, and follows continued scrutiny of whether TrumpRx, the Trump administration's most-favored-nation pricing platform launched in February, actually beats what patients already pay through insurance. A recent member survey by the Academy of Managed Care Pharmacy (AMCP) reported widespread skepticism among managed care professionals on that question, as
Pharmaceutical Commerce
previously reported
.
3
How Would the Price Comparison Feature Work?
Under the commitment, RTBTs used by prescribers will display the TrumpRx cash price for a drug next to the cost associated with filling the prescription under the patient's plan benefit at a pharmacy.
1
PBMs already use RTBTs to show doctors a range of treatment costs. The new element folds TrumpRx's cash-pay pricing into that same comparison.
In a statement to
Pharmaceutical Commerce
, Adam Colborn, vice president of government affairs at the AMCP, said the move addresses a real information gap, but noted it leans on a system with a documented adoption problem.
“This is a helpful move by managed care to facilitate patients’ ability to shop for the best price, but it’s dependent on patients’ access to real-time benefit tools,” Colborn said.
4
How Often Do Physicians Actually Use RTBTs?
According to Colborn, RTBTs are effective at reducing patient costs when used, “but doctors rarely use them.” Physicians report opening the RTBT in only 1.3% to 13.5% of encounters, and when the RTBT suggests a change, doctors accept it in only 11% of cases, he added.
5,6
All major PBMs offer RTBTs, and are mandated to do so in Part D, but only 55% of hospitals report using it for all or nearly all plans as of 2025.
7
Further, employers sometimes do not opt in to the technology, Colborn said.
“When enabled, price comparison tools are typically available to patients through their insurance portals. Because prescriptions are usually sent to pharmacies while the patient is still in their doctor’s office, they may not use the tool in their patient portal,” he added.
“Ultimately, this is an improvement to RTBTs, but doctors’ infrequent use of the tool will limit its impact,” Colborn said.
What Does AMCP's Survey Show About Real-World Confidence?
AMCP's June 2026 member survey, which drew 59 anonymous responses from health plans, PBMs, integrated delivery networks and consulting firms, surfaced doubt about whether TrumpRx beats insurance-based pricing.
3
When asked how likely an insured patient is to find medication on TrumpRx at a lower cost than through insurance, given that across the board, TrumpRx purchases do not count toward a deductible, 21 respondents said unlikely, compared with 11 who said likely or very likely and 17 who were neutral.
3
When asked more broadly how likely the TrumpRx platform is to lower US prescription drug costs overall, 26 respondents said unlikely and 18 said very unlikely, versus 11 who said likely or very likely.
What Does This Mean for Manufacturers' Channel Strategy?
For manufacturers with TrumpRx pricing agreements, the RTBT change puts a cash-pay price in direct, side-by-side view against the same product's negotiated formulary price at the moment a prescriber is deciding what to write. That visibility cuts both ways. A manufacturer whose
TrumpRx cash price undercuts a payer's benefit-based cost
could see prescribers and patients steered toward the cash channel, a dynamic that sits outside the rebate and formulary structure manufacturers negotiate with PBMs. Manufacturers without a TrumpRx deal get no comparable exposure in the tool.
The physician-adoption data Colborn cited suggests that exposure will be limited in the near term, and the practical effect of the commitment on any single manufacturer's channel mix will depend heavily on which prescribers' systems have adopted the tool and how it's configured there.
Whether the new price display changes prescribing behavior at scale depends on the same physician workflow constraints Colborn and the RTBT literature describe: display rates in the single digits to low teens, acceptance rates near 11% when a suggestion does appear and inconsistent employer opt-in even where the technology exists.

Pharma Associations.content:
Neolpharma to Expand Drug Production in Mexico
21.08.2026
Sofía Ortiz
bottom1
Drug production
Mexico
Neolpharma
The International Finance Corporation (IFC), a member of the World Bank Group, will provide financing to Neolpharma to expand its pharmaceutical manufacturing capacity in Mexico, through projects aimed at increasing local production of active pharmaceutical ingredients and injectable medications, as well as creating approximately 600 skilled jobs once the new operations reach full capacity.
Neolpharma’s capacity expansion is expected to increase domestic production and strengthen the security of supply in the energy sector linked to the healthcare system. “This investment represents a decisive step toward strengthening Mexico’s pharmaceutical capacity and expanding the population’s access to affordable, high-quality medicines,” said Astrea Ocampo, CEO of the Neolpharma Group.
He also added that the company hopes to continue investing in innovation, local manufacturing, and specialized talent.
Meanwhile, Saana Abouzaid, IFC’s regional director for Mexico, Central America, and the Dominican Republic, explained that strengthening local pharmaceutical manufacturing is essential to improving access to medicines and bolstering the resilience of supply chains, noting also that the project will help drive innovation, competitiveness, and economic growth in Mexico.
It is important to note that the transaction includes a mechanism that links the terms of the loan to the employment of people with disabilities. Neolpharma could qualify for a reduction in the financing spread if it meets the agreed-upon targets for professional training and employment opportunities for this group. This is the IFC’s first investment worldwide to incorporate a performance indicator of this kind.
The new injectable drug plant plans to seek EDGE Advanced certification and implement energy- and water-efficiency measures. With Neolpharma’s expansion, Mexico will add industrial capacity to the sector where domestic production is growing, helping to reduce reliance on foreign sources and strengthening the pharmaceutical supply chain to expand opportunities for specialized manufacturing talent.

Polyester Shrink Bands Market to Reach 170 Index by 2035 on Biopharma Capacity Expansion
Abstract
According to the latest IndexBox report on the global
Polyester Shrink Bands market
, the market enters 2026 with broader demand fundamentals, more disciplined procurement behavior, and a more regionally diversified supply architecture.
The global polyester shrink bands market is set to record sustained expansion over the 2026-2035 forecast period, supported by tightening regulatory frameworks for tamper-evident packaging and rising demand from pharmaceutical and biopharmaceutical production. Polyester shrink bands, heat-shrinkable sleeves made from polyester film, are widely used for tamper-evident sealing, labeling, and bundling of containers across food and beverage, pharmaceuticals, cosmetics, and household chemicals. The market is projected to grow at a compound annual rate of 5-7% from 2026 to 2035, driven primarily by expanding pharmaceutical and biopharma production capacity, stricter tamper-evident regulations, and increasing adoption of monoclonal antibody and cell/gene therapy packaging requirements. Pharmaceutical end-use accounts for an estimated 65-75% of global demand, with the remaining share split among nutraceuticals, specialty reagents, and life-science tools, reflecting the product's critical role in securing drug product integrity and brand authentication on primary containers. More than 40% of worldwide supply is sourced from manufacturing clusters in East Asia (China, India, Southeast Asia), with significant import dependencies in North America and Europe, where regulatory documentation and supplier qualification represent the primary procurement bottleneck. Demand is shifting toward higher-specification bands with validated UV resistance, controlled shrinkage ratios, and low-oligomer content to meet stringent biopharma and cell-therapy sterilization and cold-chain requirements; premium grades now represent roughly 25-30% of total procurement value. The baseline scenario for the polyester shrink bands market points to a compound annual growth rate of approximately 5.8% from 2026 to 2035, with the market index reaching 170 by 2035 (2025=100). This growth is underpinned by structural demand from the pharmaceutical and biopharmaceutical sectors, where polyester shrink bands are essential for tamper-evident sealing, brand protection, and compliance with serialization mandates. The market is characterized by a high degree of regulatory scrutiny, with buyers requiring documented supplier qualification, validated shrink performance, and consistent dimensional tolerances. As a result, the competitive landscape favors established converters with proven quality systems and the ability to supply dedicated production lines for pharma clients. Over the forecast period, demand will be further supported by the expansion of biologic drug manufacturing, including monoclonal antibodies and cell and gene therapies, which require specialized packaging solutions that maintain sterility and integrity under cold-chain conditions. The shift toward higher-specification bands, including UV-resistant and low-oligomer grades, is expected to continue, with premium products capturing a larger share of procurement value. However, the market faces challenges from feedstock price volatility, particularly for PETG copolyester and specialty polyester resins, which represent 55-65% of finished band production cost. Capacity constraints at qualified manufacturing sites, coupled with lead times of 18-24 months for capacity expansion, may limit supply growth. Demand Structure by End-Use Industry
Pharmaceuticals (estimated share: 70%)
Pharmaceuticals represent the dominant end-use segment for polyester shrink bands, accounting for an estimated 70% of global demand. The segment is driven by regulatory mandates such as the FDA Drug Supply Chain Security Act and the EU Falsified Medicines Directive, which require tamper-evident packaging and product serialization. Polyester shrink bands are used on vials, bottles, and syringes to provide a secure seal that indicates tampering and ensures product integrity. Through 2035, the segment will benefit from the expansion of biologic drug manufacturing, including monoclonal antibodies and cell and gene therapies, which require specialized packaging that maintains sterility under cold-chain conditions. Demand-side indicators include the number of approved biologic drugs, pharmaceutical production volumes, and the rate of packaging line automation. The trend toward higher-specification bands with UV resistance and low-oligomer content is expected to continue, as these properties are critical for maintaining drug stability and compliance with stringent regulatory standards. Current trend: Increasing adoption of serialization and tamper-evident features.
Major trends:
Serialization and anti-counterfeiting mandates, Growth in biologic and cell/gene therapy packaging, Shift to premium grades with validated performance, and Automation of packaging lines.
Representative participants:
Pfizer Inc, Novartis AG, Roche Holding AG, Johnson & Johnson, and Merck & Co., Inc.
Nutraceuticals (estimated share: 12%)
Nutraceuticals, including dietary supplements and vitamins, account for approximately 12% of polyester shrink band demand. This segment is driven by increasing consumer focus on health and wellness, leading to higher production volumes of supplements in bottles and jars. Polyester shrink bands are used for tamper-evident sealing and to provide a premium appearance that enhances brand perception. The segment is expected to grow steadily through 2035, supported by the expansion of e-commerce sales, which require secure packaging to prevent tampering during transit. Demand-side indicators include the number of new supplement launches, retail sales growth, and the adoption of child-resistant packaging. The trend toward clean-label and sustainable packaging is prompting manufacturers to switch from PVC to polyester bands, which are more recyclable and have a lower environmental footprint. Major companies in this segment are investing in high-quality printing and customization to differentiate their products on crowded shelves. Current trend: Rising demand for premium and secure packaging.
Major trends:
Growth in e-commerce and direct-to-consumer sales, Shift to sustainable and recyclable materials, Premiumization of packaging design, and Increased focus on child-resistant features.
Representative participants:
Nature's Bounty Co, Herbalife Nutrition Ltd, GNC Holdings, Inc, Amway Corporation, and Abbott Laboratories.
Specialty Reagents (estimated share: 8%)
Specialty reagents, including laboratory chemicals and diagnostic reagents, represent about 8% of polyester shrink band demand. This segment requires packaging that ensures product integrity and prevents contamination, making polyester shrink bands an ideal choice due to their chemical resistance and dimensional stability. The growth of the life sciences and diagnostics sectors, particularly in emerging markets, is driving demand for secure packaging solutions. Through 2035, the segment will benefit from the expansion of research and development activities in biopharmaceuticals and the increasing use of reagents in point-of-care testing. Demand-side indicators include the number of research laboratories, diagnostic test volumes, and the adoption of single-use technologies. The trend toward higher-specification bands with low oligomer content and validated UV resistance is expected to continue, as these properties are critical for maintaining reagent stability and compliance with regulatory standards. Major companies are focusing on establishing qualified supplier relationships to ensure consistent quality and supply security. Current trend: Increasing demand for high-purity and contamination-free packaging.
Major trends:
Expansion of life sciences research, Growth in point-of-care diagnostics, Demand for high-purity packaging materials, and Supplier qualification and long-term agreements.
Representative participants:
Thermo Fisher Scientific Inc, Merck KGaA, Danaher Corporation, Bio-Rad Laboratories, Inc, and Agilent Technologies, Inc.
Life-Science Tools (estimated share: 6%)
Life-science tools, including laboratory equipment and consumables, account for approximately 6% of polyester shrink band demand. This segment uses polyester shrink bands for tamper-evident sealing of cryovials, sample bags, and single-use bioprocessing containers. The growth of cell and gene therapy workflows is driving demand for secure and sterile packaging solutions that can withstand cryogenic temperatures and maintain integrity during storage and transport. Through 2035, the segment will benefit from the increasing adoption of single-use technologies in biopharmaceutical manufacturing, which require reliable sealing solutions. Demand-side indicators include the number of cell and gene therapy clinical trials, bioprocessing capacity expansions, and the adoption of automated packaging systems. The trend toward higher-specification bands with controlled shrinkage ratios and low extractables is expected to continue, as these properties are critical for ensuring product safety and regulatory compliance. Major companies are investing in product innovation to meet the evolving needs of the life-science tools market. Current trend: Adoption of polyester bands in single-use systems and cryovials.
Major trends:
Growth in cell and gene therapy workflows, Adoption of single-use bioprocessing systems, Demand for cryogenic-compatible packaging, and Automation of laboratory packaging processes.
Representative participants:
Sartorius AG, Thermo Fisher Scientific Inc, Corning Incorporated, Lonza Group AG, and Cytiva (Danaher Corporation).
Other End-Uses (estimated share: 4%)
Other end-uses, including cosmetics, personal care, and household chemicals, account for the remaining 4% of polyester shrink band demand. This segment uses polyester shrink bands for tamper-evident sealing and decorative labeling on bottles and jars. The growth of the cosmetics industry, particularly in Asia-Pacific, is driving demand for high-quality packaging that enhances brand image and ensures product safety. Through 2035, the segment will benefit from the increasing consumer preference for premium and sustainable packaging, prompting manufacturers to switch from PVC to polyester bands. Demand-side indicators include the number of new product launches, retail sales growth, and the adoption of eco-friendly packaging materials. The trend toward customization and high-quality printing is expected to continue, as brands seek to differentiate themselves in a competitive market. Major companies are focusing on developing bands with enhanced aesthetic appeal and functional properties, such as UV resistance and moisture resistance, to meet the evolving needs of this segment. Current trend: Diversification into cosmetics and household chemicals.
Major trends:
Premiumization of cosmetic packaging, Shift to sustainable materials, Customization and high-quality printing, and Growth in Asia-Pacific cosmetics market.
Representative participants:
L'Oréal S.A, The Procter & Gamble Company, Unilever PLC, Estée Lauder Companies Inc, and Shiseido Company, Limited.

Regional Dynamics
Asia-Pacific (estimated share: 45%)
Asia-Pacific dominates the polyester shrink bands market, driven by large-scale manufacturing in China, India, and Southeast Asia. The region is a major production hub, with over 40% of global supply sourced from East Asian clusters. Demand is supported by expanding pharmaceutical and consumer goods industries, as well as increasing regulatory focus on packaging integrity. Growth is expected to outpace the global average through 2035. Direction: up.
North America (estimated share: 25%)
North America is a significant consumer of polyester shrink bands, with demand driven by strict FDA regulations and a well-established pharmaceutical sector. The region relies heavily on imports, with supplier qualification being a key procurement bottleneck. Growth is expected to be steady, supported by the expansion of biologic drug manufacturing and the adoption of serialization requirements. Direction: stable.
Europe (estimated share: 20%)
Europe is a mature market for polyester shrink bands, with demand driven by EU regulations on tamper-evident packaging and anti-counterfeiting. The region has a strong pharmaceutical industry and a growing focus on sustainable packaging solutions. Growth is expected to be moderate, with increasing adoption of recyclable polyester bands over PVC alternatives. Direction: stable.
Latin America (estimated share: 6%)
Latin America is an emerging market for polyester shrink bands, with demand driven by the expansion of the pharmaceutical and food and beverage industries. The region is seeing increasing regulatory scrutiny on packaging integrity, which is expected to boost demand for tamper-evident solutions. Growth is projected to be above the global average, albeit from a small base. Direction: up.
Middle East & Africa (estimated share: 4%)
The Middle East and Africa region is a small but growing market for polyester shrink bands, supported by the development of local pharmaceutical manufacturing and increasing import of packaged goods. Demand is driven by the need for secure packaging in hot climates, where polyester bands offer superior performance compared to PVC. Growth is expected to be steady, with opportunities in emerging markets. Direction: up.

Collapsible Transfer Containers Market to Surpass USD 3.8B by 2035 on Single-Use Biopharma Shift
Abstract
According to the latest IndexBox report on the global
Collapsible Transfer Containers market
, the market enters 2026 with broader demand fundamentals, more disciplined procurement behavior, and a more regionally diversified supply architecture.
The world collapsible transfer containers market is entering a phase of sustained expansion, with demand projected to rise at a compound annual growth rate of 11–14% from 2026 to 2035. This growth is underpinned by the accelerating shift toward single-use technologies in biopharmaceutical manufacturing, where collapsible containers serve as critical sterile interfaces for transferring media, buffers, intermediates, and final drug products. The market, valued at approximately USD 1.2 billion in 2025, is expected to surpass USD 3.8 billion by 2035, supported by capacity additions in emerging biomanufacturing hubs across Asia-Pacific and Latin America. Biopharmaceutical manufacturing and cell & gene therapy workflows together account for over 70% of global demand, with premium-grade, pre-validated containers representing the fastest-growing price tier. Supply remains concentrated among a small number of qualified manufacturers in North America and Western Europe, creating import dependence in regions where bioprocess capacity is expanding most rapidly. Key trends include the adoption of ready-to-use container systems integrated with automated filling platforms, custom geometries with enhanced oxygen barrier properties, and a growing emphasis on recyclable materials. However, supplier qualification cycles of 12–24 months and regulatory harmonization gaps continue to shape market dynamics, favoring established players with robust documentation portfolios.
The baseline scenario for the collapsible transfer containers market points to robust growth through 2035, with the market index rising from 100 in 2025 to approximately 330 by 2035, reflecting a CAGR of 12.5%. This trajectory is supported by the continued expansion of single-use bioprocessing capacity, particularly in Asia-Pacific, where new biologics manufacturing facilities are coming online at an unprecedented pace. Demand for collapsible containers is closely tied to biopharmaceutical production volumes, which are growing at 8–10% annually, and to the penetration of single-use systems, which is expected to rise from 45% of bioprocessing operations in 2025 to over 65% by 2035. The market is also benefiting from the increasing complexity of biologics, including cell and gene therapies, which require highly controlled, sterile transfer processes. On the supply side, manufacturers are investing in multi-layer film technologies that reduce leachables and improve oxygen barriers, while also addressing sustainability pressures by developing containers with reduced plastic mass and recyclable components. However, the market faces constraints from lengthy qualification cycles, raw material price volatility, and incomplete regulatory harmonization, which may temper growth in the near term. Overall, the outlook remains positive, with demand expected to accelerate by 2035 as new applications emerge in decentralized manufacturing and personalized medicine.
Demand Drivers and Constraints
Primary Demand Drivers
Rapid adoption of single-use technologies in biopharmaceutical manufacturing
Expansion of cell and gene therapy workflows requiring sterile transfer systems
Increasing bioprocess capacity in Asia-Pacific and Latin America
Demand for pre-validated, ready-to-use container systems to reduce qualification lead times
Growing need for custom container geometries and multilayer films with improved barrier properties
Sustainability initiatives pushing for reduced plastic mass and recyclable components
Potential Growth Constraints
Supplier qualification cycles of 12–24 months for regulated end users
Input cost volatility for specialty polymer resins and EVOH barrier layers
Incomplete regulatory harmonization across FDA, EMA, and emerging pharmacopoeias
Technical challenges in material substitution due to validation requirements
Supply chain concentration in North America and Western Europe leading to import dependence
Demand Structure by End-Use Industry
Bioprocessing and Drug Manufacturing (estimated share: 55%)
Bioprocessing and drug manufacturing is the largest end-use segment, accounting for 55% of global demand. This segment relies on collapsible transfer containers for sterile transfer of cell culture media, buffers, intermediates, and final drug product between bioreactors, hold tanks, filtration skids, and fill-finish lines. The shift from stainless steel to single-use systems is a key driver, as collapsible containers reduce cross-contamination risks, eliminate cleaning validation, and lower water and energy consumption. Through 2035, demand will be supported by the expansion of biologics manufacturing capacity, particularly for monoclonal antibodies and biosimilars, with new facilities in Asia-Pacific and Latin America. Demand-side indicators include biopharmaceutical production volumes, number of approved biologics, and capacity utilization rates. The trend toward continuous manufacturing and intensified processes will increase the need for reliable, high-performance containers with low extractable profiles. Major companies in this segment include Thermo Fisher Scientific, Sartorius AG, and Merck KGaA, which supply pre-validated systems that integrate with automated platforms. Current trend: Dominant segment with steady volume growth as single-use systems become standard in biologics production.
Major trends:
Shift from stainless steel to single-use systems, Adoption of continuous manufacturing processes, Integration with automated filling and transfer platforms, and Development of multilayer films with enhanced barrier properties.
Representative participants:
Thermo Fisher Scientific, Sartorius AG, Merck KGaA, Pall Corporation, and Entegris, Inc.
Cell and Gene Therapy Workflows (estimated share: 18%)
Cell and gene therapy workflows represent 18% of global demand and are the fastest-growing segment, driven by the increasing number of approved therapies and clinical trials. These therapies require highly controlled, sterile transfer of cells, viral vectors, and gene-editing reagents, where collapsible containers with custom geometries and low leachable/extractable profiles are essential. The demand is particularly strong for small-volume, single-use containers that can be integrated into closed processing systems, reducing contamination risks and improving patient safety. Through 2035, the segment will benefit from the commercialization of new therapies, especially in oncology and rare diseases, and from the expansion of manufacturing capacity by CDMOs. Key demand-side indicators include the number of approved cell and gene therapies, clinical trial activity, and investment in manufacturing infrastructure. The trend toward decentralized manufacturing and point-of-care production will create new opportunities for flexible, scalable container solutions. Major companies include Sartorius AG, Thermo Fisher Scientific, and Charter Medical, which offer specialized containers for viral vector production and cell processing. Current trend: Fastest-growing segment with demand for high-purity, custom-designed containers for sensitive therapies.
Major trends:
Commercialization of new cell and gene therapies, Adoption of closed processing systems, Growth of decentralized and point-of-care manufacturing, and Demand for custom geometries and low-extractable films.
Representative participants:
Sartorius AG, Thermo Fisher Scientific, Charter Medical, Ltd, Meissner Filtration Products, and Aseptic Technologies.
Research and Development (estimated share: 12%)
Research and development accounts for 12% of global demand, driven by the need for flexible, cost-effective containers in process development, scale-up studies, and academic research. Collapsible containers are used in R&D settings for media preparation, buffer storage, and small-scale bioprocessing experiments, where ease of use and disposability are valued. The segment is supported by increasing investment in biopharmaceutical R&D, particularly in emerging markets, and by the trend toward open innovation and collaborative research. Through 2035, demand will grow as new modalities, such as mRNA and viral vectors, require specialized containers for research and early-stage manufacturing. Key demand-side indicators include R&D spending by biopharma companies, number of research institutions, and grant funding. The trend toward automation and high-throughput screening will increase the need for standardized, pre-validated containers that can be used across different platforms. Major companies include Thermo Fisher Scientific, Merck KGaA, and Danaher Corporation, which offer a wide range of R&D-grade consumables. Current trend: Steady demand from academic and industrial R&D labs for flexible scale-up and process development.
Major trends:
Increased R&D spending in biopharmaceuticals, Adoption of high-throughput screening and automation, Growth of mRNA and viral vector research, and Demand for standardized, pre-validated containers.
Representative participants:
Thermo Fisher Scientific, Merck KGaA, Danaher Corporation, Sartorius AG, and Entegris, Inc.
Quality Control and Release Testing (estimated share: 10%)
Quality control and release testing represents 10% of global demand, driven by the need for validated, contamination-free containers for sampling, sample storage, and analytical testing. These containers must meet stringent regulatory requirements for leachables and extractables, as they come into contact with drug products and intermediates. The segment is growing in line with the expansion of biopharmaceutical manufacturing and the increasing complexity of regulatory requirements. Through 2035, demand will be supported by the adoption of continuous quality monitoring and real-time release testing, which require reliable, single-use sampling systems. Key demand-side indicators include the number of batch releases, regulatory inspection activity, and the adoption of process analytical technology (PAT). The trend toward integrated quality systems and digitalization will increase the need for containers with traceability features, such as RFID tags and barcodes. Major companies include Pall Corporation, Sartorius AG, and Meissner Filtration Products, which offer QC-grade containers and sampling systems. Current trend: Growing demand for validated containers used in QC labs for sample handling and analytical testing.
Major trends:
Adoption of continuous quality monitoring, Integration of traceability features like RFID, Growth of process analytical technology (PAT), and Increasing regulatory scrutiny on leachables and extractables.
Representative participants:
Pall Corporation, Sartorius AG, Meissner Filtration Products, Thermo Fisher Scientific, and Entegris, Inc.
Other Industrial Applications (estimated share: 5%)
Other industrial applications account for 5% of global demand, including use in food and beverage processing, chemical manufacturing, and water treatment. In these sectors, collapsible containers are used for the storage and transport of liquid ingredients, additives, and intermediate products, offering advantages in space efficiency and reduced shipping costs. The segment is relatively mature, with growth tied to industrial production volumes and trade flows. Through 2035, demand will be supported by the increasing adoption of flexible packaging solutions and the need for cost-effective bulk transport. Key demand-side indicators include industrial production indices, trade volumes, and the expansion of food processing capacity in emerging markets. The trend toward sustainability is driving interest in reusable collapsible containers, which reduce waste and lower lifecycle costs. Major companies include Saint-Gobain Performance Plastics and Flex Concepts, which supply industrial-grade containers for non-pharmaceutical applications. Current trend: Niche but stable demand from food, beverage, and chemical industries for flexible bulk storage and transport.
Major trends:
Adoption of flexible packaging in food and beverage, Growth of reusable container systems, Expansion of chemical and water treatment industries, and Focus on reducing shipping costs and storage space.
Representative participants:
Saint-Gobain Performance Plastics, Flex Concepts, Inc, Advanced Scientific, and Charter Medical, Ltd.
